title: Data Quality

toc.title: Data Quality Process: PDCA / Shewhart Cycle

html:
1Definition and Goals

Definition: Planning, implementation, and control activities applied to data to ensure it is fit for purpose for data consumers.

Alternative Phrase: Data is "fit for purpose" — fitness for use relative to the intended use.

DAMA Definition: The planning, implementation, and control of activities that apply quality management techniques to data, in order to assure it is fit for consumption and meets the needs of data consumers.

3 Goals:

  1. Develop a managed approach to making data fit for purpose
  2. Define data quality requirements based on the needs of data consumers
  3. Identify and correct defects in data and processes that create defective data

2Business Drivers

  • Poor data quality costs organizations significant money (Gartner estimated $9.7M/year per organization)
  • Regulatory compliance requires high quality data
  • Unreliable data undermines trust and slows decision-making
  • Data quality directly impacts operational efficiency and customer satisfaction
  • Required for successful analytics, MDM, and data governance initiatives

3Nine Guiding Principles

  1. Data quality is everyone's concern — not just the IT department
  2. Data quality requires proactive management — prevention better than correction
  3. Data must be fit for purpose — quality defined relative to intended use, not absolute standard
  4. Define requirements based on consumer needs — understand how consumers use data
  5. Data is produced through processes — root causes in processes, not just data
  6. Manage at the source — fix quality at the point of creation
  7. Continuous improvement — quality improvement is ongoing, not a one-time project
  8. Data quality requires organizational commitment — needs executive support and resources
  9. Data quality enables trust — high quality data increases confidence in decision-making

4Data Quality Dimensions

Strong and Wang (1996) Framework — 15 Dimensions in 4 Categories

Category Dimensions
Intrinsic DQ Accuracy, Objectivity, Believability, Reputation
Contextual DQ Relevancy, Completeness, Timeliness, Appropriate Amount, Value-Added
Representational DQ Interpretability, Format, Ease of Understanding, Concise Representation, Consistent Representation
Accessibility DQ Accessibility, Access Security

DAMA UK (2013) — 6 Core Dimensions

Dimension Definition
Completeness Proportion of stored data against the potential of 100% complete
Uniqueness No entity is recorded more than once based upon business rules
Timeliness Data represents reality from the required point in time
Validity Data conforms to syntax (format, type, range) defined by business rules
Accuracy Data correctly describes the real-world object it represents
Consistency No conflict between two values that both relate to the same fact across different systems
Exam tip

DAMA UK 6 = the most commonly referenced DQ dimension set for CDMP fundamentals.

ISO 8000

International standard for data quality; focuses on data exchange and characterization of data quality.

5Data Quality Measurement

Measurement Formulas

Valid Records: $$\text{DQ Score} = \frac{\text{Valid Records}}{\text{Total Records}} \times 100%$$

Invalid/Exception Rate: $$\text{Exception Rate} = \frac{\text{Records with Exceptions}}{\text{Total Records}} \times 100%$$

Example: If 950 of 1,000 records pass a quality rule → DQ Score = 95%, Exception Rate = 5%

Data Profiling

Definition: Statistical examination of data to understand its structure, content, and quality.

Profiling Activities:

  • Column analysis — min/max values, null counts, distinct values, data type conformance
  • Cross-column analysis — dependency analysis, correlations
  • Cross-table analysis — referential integrity, orphan records
  • Pattern analysis — format consistency, value distribution

6Nine Business Rule Types

Rule Type Description Example
Definition What an entity or attribute is "Customer" is a person who has purchased in the last 24 months
Structural How data must be structured Address must have street, city, postal code
Domain Valid values for an attribute Status must be "Active," "Inactive," or "Pending"
Range Valid value range Age must be between 0 and 150
Referential Integrity Foreign key relationships Order must reference a valid Customer
Uniqueness No duplicates allowed Social Security Number must be unique per customer
Completeness Required fields First Name cannot be null
Derivation Calculated values Total = Quantity × Unit Price
Trigger Conditional rules If customer is VIP, discount must be applied

7Data Quality Process: PDCA / Shewhart Cycle

Shewhart Cycle (1920s manufacturing) → adopted by Deming → PDCA:

Phase Activities
Plan Identify data quality issues; assess impact; set quality targets; develop quality rules
Do Implement data quality rules and controls; cleanse data; apply corrections
Check Measure data quality; monitor trends; compare against targets
Act Investigate root causes; implement process improvements; prevent recurrence

Origin: PDCA was developed by Walter Shewhart in the 1920s for manufacturing; W. Edwards Deming popularized it for quality management.

8Root Cause Analysis

Purpose: Identify the underlying causes of data quality issues to prevent recurrence.

Common Root Causes:

  • Missing or inadequate data entry validation
  • Poor process design — data captured at wrong point or in wrong form
  • System migrations — data transformation errors
  • Organizational changes — business rules changed without updating systems
  • No data stewardship — no accountability for data quality
  • Technical issues — system bugs, encoding problems

Techniques:

  • 5 Whys — ask "why" five times to uncover root cause
  • Ishikawa (fishbone) diagram — visualize cause-and-effect relationships
  • Pareto Analysis — identify the 20% of causes responsible for 80% of problems

9Statistical Process Control (SPC)

Origin: 1920s manufacturing (Walter Shewhart) Application: Monitoring data quality over time using control charts.

Key Concepts:

  • Control Charts — plot measurements over time; show process stability
  • Control Limits — upper and lower bounds; 3 sigma (standard deviations) from mean
  • Common Cause Variation — natural variation within control limits (expected)
  • Special Cause Variation — unexpected variation outside control limits (investigate)

10Data Quality Activities (6 Activity Areas)

Activity 1: Define High-Quality Data

  • Identify data consumers and understand their needs
  • Define quality requirements per consumer use case
  • Document business rules and quality criteria
  • Establish acceptable thresholds

Activity 2: Define Data Quality Strategy

  • Assess current DQ maturity
  • Define governance structure for DQ
  • Select tools and approaches
  • Build business case

Activity 3: Identify Critical Data and Business Rules

  • Identify Critical Data Elements (CDEs) — most important data for business decisions
  • Document business rules associated with CDEs
  • Prioritize based on business impact

Activity 4: Perform an Initial Data Quality Assessment

  • Profile data against business rules
  • Identify and quantify data quality issues
  • Document findings with business impact
  • Prioritize issues for remediation

Activity 5: Identify and Prioritize Potential Improvements

  • Root cause analysis of identified issues
  • Define remediation approach (correction vs. prevention)
  • Prioritize by business impact and feasibility

Activity 6: Define and Implement Data Quality Controls

  • Build data quality rules into source processes
  • Implement automated DQ monitoring
  • Create exception reporting
  • Establish feedback loops to data producers

11Data Quality Tools

Tool Type Purpose
Data Profiling Tools Statistical analysis of data content; identify anomalies
Data Parsing and Standardization Correct format inconsistencies; standardize values
Data Matching Identify duplicate or near-duplicate records
Data Cleansing / Remediation Correct or delete invalid records
Data Monitoring Continuously monitor quality against defined rules
Address Standardization Validate and standardize postal addresses

12Data Quality Governance

Critical Success Factors:

  • Executive sponsorship
  • Clear ownership and stewardship
  • Integration with business processes (quality at the source)
  • Defined metrics and measurement approach
  • Feedback mechanisms from consumers to producers

Data Quality Metrics:

  • Completeness rate per CDE
  • Accuracy rate per CDE
  • Timeliness of data refresh
  • Number of open DQ issues
  • DQ issue resolution time
  • Trend of DQ scores over time

DQ Scorecard:

  • Aggregates DQ metrics across dimensions and data domains
  • Provides executive visibility into data quality status
  • Should show trends over time

13Practice Q&A

Q1: What is the definition of Data Quality? A: Planning, implementation, and control activities applied to data to ensure it is fit for purpose for data consumers.

Q2: What are the 6 DAMA UK core data quality dimensions? A: Completeness, Uniqueness, Timeliness, Validity, Accuracy, Consistency.

Q3: What are the 4 categories and 15 dimensions of Strong and Wang (1996)? A: Intrinsic (Accuracy, Objectivity, Believability, Reputation), Contextual (Relevancy, Completeness, Timeliness, Appropriate Amount, Value-Added), Representational (Interpretability, Format, Ease of Understanding, Concise, Consistent Representation), Accessibility (Accessibility, Access Security).

Q4: Who developed PDCA and when? A: Walter Shewhart in the 1920s for manufacturing; W. Edwards Deming popularized it for quality management.

Q5: What does PDCA stand for? A: Plan, Do, Check, Act.

Q6: What is Statistical Process Control and what are control limits? A: SPC monitors process stability over time using control charts; control limits are 3 sigma (standard deviations) from the mean; points outside limits indicate special cause variation.

Q7: What is data profiling? A: Statistical examination of data to understand its structure, content, and quality; includes column analysis, cross-column, cross-table, and pattern analysis.

Q8: What is the formula for data quality score? A: (Valid Records / Total Records) × 100%.

Q9: What are the 9 business rule types? A: Definition, Structural, Domain, Range, Referential Integrity, Uniqueness, Completeness, Derivation, Trigger.

Q10: What is a Critical Data Element (CDE)? A: The most important data elements for business decisions; highest priority for data quality management.

Q11: What are the 3 root cause analysis techniques? A: 5 Whys, Ishikawa (fishbone) diagram, Pareto Analysis.

Q12: What is ISO 8000? A: International standard for data quality; focuses on data exchange and characterization of data quality.

Q13: What is "fitness for purpose" in data quality? A: Quality is defined relative to how the data will be used by consumers, not against an absolute standard.

Q14: What is common cause vs. special cause variation in SPC? A: Common cause = natural variation within control limits (expected); Special cause = unexpected variation outside control limits (requires investigation).

Q15: What are the 6 data quality activity areas? A: Define high-quality data, Define DQ strategy, Identify critical data/business rules, Perform initial DQ assessment, Identify/prioritize improvements, Define/implement DQ controls.

14Quick Reference
